answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 50 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is entered against the river challenge, the tide audit can replay the dune history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm thus has to pad 239 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
